acceptance: `evolve rebuild --project-root P` builds P's HEAD to the path the boot refresh uses and prints both SHAs (red: unknown command)
A live run lease exits 1; a failing build exits 2 with the output tail
The boot refresh and the verb call one build function (test)
fix: Add `evolve rebuild [--project-root P] [--repin]`. It runs the boot refresh's build step (the same make target and output path) for P's HEAD and prints the old and new binary SHAs. --repin then re-pins the ship SHA through reset-sha's provenance-gated path. A live run lease on P exits 1. A build failure exits 2 with the tail of the output. The boot refresh and the verb call one build function. Document it in runtime-reference.md and workspace-layout.md, replacing the raw make.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: The loop rebuilds and re-execs a binary behind HEAD at boot and at chain boundaries (loopchain's binary-refresh engine; runtime-reference.md:177), but nothing exposes that build. A fresh worktree, a console tree after a merge, or a plane before a boundary check needs `make -C go build` by hand (workspace-layout.md:38), and a same-version rebuild can leave the ship SHA pin stale until `evolve reset-sha`. A bare `go build` in go/ overwrites the tracked go/evolve instead.
title: Rebuilding an evolve binary outside the loop's boot refresh is `make -C go build` by hand; add `evolve rebuild`
